steps.title: The longest pattern, and the last new one
body: Form X's signature is اِسْتَ prefixed to the root, giving the shape اِسْتَفْعَلَ — the longest of the ten patterns.

اِسْتَيْقَظَ ("to wake up"), already in your vocabulary since A1, is a Form X verb — root ي-ق-ظ ("wakefulness"): اِسْتَيْقَظَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الصَّبَاحِ, "the boy woke up in the morning," present tense يَسْتَيْقِظُ.

Form X often means "to seek or consider X," or carries a reflexive-causative sense — "to render yourself X." That's eight of the ten forms now, each recognisable by its own distinct shape. Only Form IX — a doubled final letter, used almost only for colours and physical defects — stays ahead, past B1.

steps.title: Form X in one sentence
steps.intro: Read the sentence, then check what marks it as Form X. Tap 🔊 to hear it.

steps.title: Spot the pattern
steps.prompt: اِسْتَيْقَظَ (to wake up) starts with اِسْتَ. Which form is that?
steps.explanation: اِسْتَفْعَلَ prefixes اِسْتَ to the root — the same prefix you can see on اِسْتَيْقَظَ.

steps.title: Meaning tendency
steps.prompt: What tendency does Form X often carry?

options.label: "To seek or consider X," or a reflexive-causative sense — "to render yourself X"
A passive sense with no human subject ever possible
A denominative sense, always built from a noun and never from a verb

steps.explanation: Form X's اِسْتَ prefix often adds "seeking" or a reflexive-causative sense. The "no human subject" tendency belongs to Form VII, and "always from a noun" overstates every form's flexibility — several forms, including II and IV, can go either way.

steps.title: Eight forms, eight shapes
steps.prompt: Doubled middle consonant, تَ added to that same doubling, and اِنْ prefixed with no human subject — which three forms, in order?
steps.explanation: جَرَّبَ doubles its middle consonant (Form II); تَكَلَّمَ adds تَ to that same doubled pattern (Form V); اِنْفَتَحَ prefixes اِنْ and never takes a human subject (Form VII) — three of the eight shapes you've now met.

steps.title: b1-u1 is complete
steps.message: Eight of the ten derived forms, each in its own lesson, built from a mix of words you already knew and a few new ones chosen to sit naturally beside them. Only Form IX — colours and physical defects, a genuinely rare pattern — is still ahead, and it's staying there until much later.
